mock.title: Title of the dialog. A mock server answers requests with saved examples.
mock.running: Badge shown while the server runs.
mock.noRoutesTitle: Empty state when no saved requests have examples.
mock.noMatch: Shown in the log when a request matched no route.
mock.logNoExample: Log line: the request {{name}} matched a route that has no example.
mock.scope: Choice of which requests the server answers.
mock.portTitle: Tooltip of the port field. 127.0.0.1 is the local address and stays as written.
mock.routeColumns: Column headings of the routes table.
mock.routeSwitch: Accessible name of the switch that turns a route on or off.
mock.exampleFor: Accessible name of the picker for the example a route returns.
mock.routeBehavior: Accessible name of the button that opens the delay and failure settings of a route.
mock.specTitle: Heading of the area where an OpenAPI spec adds routes.
mock.specUntitled: Used instead of the spec title when it has none.
mock.specLoaded: {{title}} is the title of the spec; {{count}} routes were created from it.
mock.rulesHint: Rules answer before the saved examples do.
mock.ruleName: Accessible name of the rule name field.
mock.ruleSwitch: Accessible name of the switch that turns a rule on or off.
mock.methodLabel: Label of the HTTP method picker of a rule.
mock.anyMethod: Option that matches every HTTP method.
mock.pathPlaceholder: Example path template; /pets/:id is code. The text in parentheses explains an empty field.
mock.when: Heading before the conditions of a rule.
mock.conditionField: Accessible name of the choice between query, header and body.
mock.conditionName: Placeholder: a query or header name, or a JSON path in the body.
mock.conditionOp: Accessible name of the operator choice.
mock.fields: Where a condition looks: the query string, a header or the body.
mock.bodyWhole: JSONPath such as $.user.name stays as written.
mock.respond: Heading before the response a rule sends.
mock.statusPlaceholder: Placeholder: the status of the route is used.
mock.headersLabel: One header per line in the form Name: value; keep that form.
mock.bodyLabel: An empty body keeps the body of the route.
mock.bodyHint: {{placeholders}} is a list of template placeholders with double braces; keep the parameter.
mock.nth: Option to answer only the Nth matching request, for example the third.
mock.nthPlaceholder: Placeholder when no number is set.
mock.inherit: Shown on a route that has no behavior of its own.
mock.cors: CORS is the browser mechanism for cross-origin requests; keep the abbreviation.
mock.corsHint: --cors-origin is a command line option and stays as written.
mock.delayMax: Upper end of a random wait range, in milliseconds.
mock.slowBody: Time over which the body is spread, in milliseconds.
mock.faultRate: Share of requests that fail on purpose, as a percentage.
mock.faultKind: Label of the kind of failure.
mock.logCount: Label of the number of logged requests.
mock.logDuration: Duration of a request in milliseconds.
mock.logBody: Size of a request body in bytes.
mock.routeSummary: Counts shown under the routes list.
mock.port: Label of the field for a network port number.
mock.start: Button that starts the mock server. Verb.
mock.stop: Button that stops the mock server. Verb.
mock.tabs.log: Tab name: the list of requests the mock server received. Noun.
mock.remove: Button that removes a rule or one of its conditions. Verb.
mock.conditionValue: Label of the field for the value a condition compares with.
mock.status: Label of the field for the HTTP status code the mock answers with.
mock.clear: Button that empties the log of received requests. Verb.
